free_tier.stated: Snippets are git repositories that count toward the namespace storage size. No limit exists on how many snippets you can create. The default maximum size for a snippet is 50 MB, and a snippet repository is limited to 10 files.

per_object_cap.stated: The default maximum size for a snippet is 50 MB. A snippet repository is limited to 10 files.
per_object_cap.notes: The snippets page gives the default maximum snippet size as current as of 2024-04-17, and links the administration page for the setting.

retention.notes: Snippets use version control: each snippet has its own underlying repository, and each saved change records a new commit. No expiry period is stated on the page.

egress.terms: unverified: no egress charge or volume quota is stated on the pages read. Public snippets can be cloned, and their raw content can be downloaded.

tooling: Snippets API (POST /snippets), git clone of the snippet repo, glab CLI, VS Code extension. Rate limited to 300 creates/hour/authenticated user.
chaining: No limits exist as to how many snippets you can create. Versioned snippets are considered part of the namespace storage size, so snippets are not a separate storage pool.
limits_note: Creating snippets is limited to 300 requests every hour for each authenticated user, shared with creating a project snippet and the createSnippet GraphQL mutation.
reliability_note: Snippets are visible/searchable by other users when public; storage is accounted at namespace level so it is the most likely subject to be capped first if GitLab ever enforces namespace quotas.

evidence.quote: The default [maximum size for a snippet](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/snippets/) and current (as of 2024-04-17) is 50 MB.

evidence.proved: there is no limit on snippet count
evidence.quote: No limits exist as to how many snippets you can create.

evidence.quote: This means that all snippets get their own underlying repository initialized with a default branch at the moment the snippet is created.

evidence.proved: snippets are managed with Git, through the snippets API, and in the UI
evidence.quote: You can manage snippets with Git (because they’re [versioned](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/snippets/#versioned-snippets) by a Git repository), through the [snippets API](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/snippets/), and in the GitLab UI.
